text:
Andrew: FYI we just got a scan result from a customer (private deploy) — transitive lib 'libfastjson' flagged with CVE-2026-9999. Customer wants ETA for a patch, SBOM export, and proof of KMS key rotation/audit logs by EOD tomorrow. :eyes:
Sarah: Looking. Is this on the agent image only or also in the hosted runtime?
Andrew: Confirmed only in the on-prem agent bundle (package tree under /opt/redwood/agent). Hosted runtime not impacted.
Mike: Ok that scope narrows it. Likely a transitive from our auth proxy layer in agent. Can you drop the sample SBOM path the customer asked for?
Andrew: They asked for SPDX+json and a list of patched transitive deps. I ran the local SBOM generator: 
```
/opt/redwood/agent$ sbom-generator --format spdx-json --output sbom-agent-spdx.json
```
Sarah: Good. For remediation: priority = high for private instances using that agent. Proposed plan: 1) push quick patch to bump libfastjson to 1.2.3, 2) produce patched agent build, 3) provide SBOM and a signed checklist (SOC2-friendly) + audit logs showing KMS rotation.
Jessica: For customers on managed Dedicated we can offer a hotfix build. For private customers we should provide clear upgrade steps and a script. I'll draft an upgrade script snippet: 
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# upgrade agent deps
sudo systemctl stop redwood-agent
cd /opt/redwood/agent
./build.sh --bump libfastjson=1.2.3
sudo systemctl start redwood-agent
```
Mike: On audit evidence: KMS rotations are logged in CloudKMS. We can export rotation events and key IDs — format we usually hand over for SOC2 is a CSV with timestamp, operation, key_id, user. I'll pull the last-3-rotations for the customer's key and sign it.
Emily-legal: Please redact any internal principals and include only service account IDs per our compliance guidance. I'll need the exported CSV to attach to the SOC2 response package.
Sarah: For RBAC mitigation while patch is rolling: we can add a temporary policy to block agent telemetry endpoints from processing user-uploaded payloads (reduces exploit surface). Mike — can you add a Canary RBAC rule in the private-policy bundle and produce an audit trail?
Mike: Yep. I'll add rule `deny:agent:payload_inspect` scoped to the affected customer org id, and enable Audit-level logging for the next 72h. sec-bot: Created SEC-2026 ticket and assigned to eng-security. Link: (sec-tracker/SEC-2026) :white_check_mark:
Andrew: ETA targets: quick lib bump PR by EOD today, patched agent build + test tomorrow AM, customer-facing upgrade script + SBOM + KMS rotation export by EOD tomorrow. Is that feasible? :thumbsup:
Sarah: Feasible. I'll own the evidence bundle (SBOM spdx json, rotation csv, audit logs snippet, and short remediation notes). Emily-legal: I'll review before we send.
Jessica: I'll prepare the customer-facing instructions and a rollback plan.
Mike: I'll push the RBAC temp rule and attach the audit events to SEC-2026.
Andrew: Thanks all — I'll update the customer with that timeline and link to SEC-2026.
sec-bot: Auto-note: vulnerability severity set to HIGH, CVSS 7.8 per internal scoring. Remediation SLA = 48h.
